pages.text: "I've never seen this green food. I won't eat it!" Mei the timid baby goat pushed greens to the edge of the plate. Yellow dandelion flowers, green leaves, and white cheese lay side by side on the long table. Mei ate only the white cheese.
"Today I'll climb to the top of the slope!" Mei pushed away the plate and hopped toward the door. The yellow and green food stayed untouched.
Halfway up, Mei's legs trembled. Even holding both orange scarf ends tightly, their feet kept sliding back. "Huh? My legs have no strength."
Soso the quiet hedgehog waved from high above. Mei sat on a rock and looked up. The top was still so far away.
Grandma Bear, who ran the lodge, sat beside Mei and pointed at the slope. "What does that yellow look like to you?" Dandelions covered the slope, with green leaves between and white snow left above.

"Your plate looked just like this slope. Yellow, green, and white all come from here." Grandma picked a yellow petal and put it in Mei's hand. "Something new? One bite!" Mei popped it in and chewed. "...Oh? Sweet!"
Back at the lodge, Mei pulled the plate close again. Crunch went the greens. A new taste, but richer than expected. "Something new? One bite!" Mei took a bite each of yellow and white too.
The next morning, Mei's legs felt light. Mei was first to step onto the rock at the top. Below, Soso hopped up the slope.
From the top, the whole village lay below. "One, something new, one bite! Two, a bite of every color! Three, then my favorites!" Soso climbed up and stood beside Mei.
Grandma lifted Mei onto her shoulders. One bite of something new can give legs strength. "Tomorrow I'll go to that peak! Something new? One bite!" Mei called.
